title: Localization of integrals of functions continuous on an open set and vanishing off a compact subset
statement: Let n be a natural number; integrals are Bochner integrals for Lebesgue measure on R^n. Let f : R^n -> R, and let O and T be subsets of R^n such that O is open, T is compact and T is contained in O. Assume that f is continuous on O (as a map restricted to O) and that f(z) = 0 for every z not in T. Then (a) f is continuous on all of R^n, (b) f is Lebesgue integrable on R^n, and (c) the integral of f over O equals the integral of f over R^n.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Rn n → ℝ) (O T : Set (Rn n)), IsOpen O → IsCompact T → T ⊆ O → ContinuousOn f O → (∀ z, z ∉ T → f z = 0) → Continuous f ∧ Integrable f ∧ ∫ z in O, f z = ∫ z, f z
